what: Mind2Web adapter validated against the real archive
why_it_matters: This adapter was the last one still verified only by a hand-written fixture. Running it on real data found two defects the fixture could not, because the fixture was written from the same wrong assumption as the adapter.

source.how: downloaded as a single parquet shard; streaming was too slow to use

bugs_found.name: the verb is the last field, not the first
bugs_found.before: action_type was the HTML tag: [button] x600, [link] x427, [input] x262
bugs_found.after: action_type is the operation: click x218, type_text x44, move x4, enter x2
bugs_found.cause: The repr is '[textbox]  US City,State or Zip Code -> TYPE: 08817'. Splitting on the first space made '[textbox]' the verb and 'US City,State or Zip Code -> TYPE: 08817' the target.
bugs_found.why_the_fixture_missed_it: The fixture used the invented shape 'CLICK [Submit]' - verb first - which is what the adapter assumed, so both agreed and both were wrong.

bugs_found.name: one row is one step, not one task
bugs_found.before: every row expanded its whole action_reprs list, 14 steps per sample
bugs_found.after: target_action_index selects the single step the row represents
bugs_found.cause: action_reprs holds the entire task; target_action_index says which step this row is. Treating the list as the trajectory multiplied each task by the length of its own action list.

bugs_found.name: the screenshot struct was dropped
bugs_found.before: image_path was None: clean_text() was applied to a struct
bugs_found.after: image_path is the real filename, and the embedded byte count is kept
bugs_found.cause: screenshot is struct<bytes: binary, path: string>, not a string.
